شَاحٍ [act. part. n. of 1: fem. شَاحِيَةٌ; pl. of the latter شَوَاحٍ and شَاحِيَاتٌ]. One says, جَآءَتِ الخَيْلُ
شَوَاحِىَ The horses came opening their mouths: (S, A, K, * TA:) and so أَقْبَلَتِ الخَيْلُ شَاحِيَاتٍ. (M, TA.) ―
-b2- And جَآءَنَا شَاحِيًا He came to us stepping along. (TA.) ―
-b3- And (assumed tropical:) He came to us without any want. (TA.) ―
-b4- الشَّوَاحِى is applied by the vulgar to The large pieces of wood resembling columns: but [SM says,] I have not seen any mention thereof in the [classical] language. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
